historical_references.reference: Arjuna is a significant character in the Indian epic Mahabharata and is the greatest warrior of the Pandava clan. He is the son of Indra and Bhargavi, and is the third of the five Pandava brothers. Arjuna's story is a major theme of the Bhagavad Gita, where he seeks the guidance of Lord Krishna on the battlefield of Kurukshetra and ultimately fulfills his dharma (duty).

Arjuna is also mentioned in the Puranas, a set of eighteen major Sanskrit texts dealing with Hindu mythology, history, and philosophy. The Arjuna-Vishnu-Samhita is a Purana dedicated to Arjuna, and recounts various tales and teachings from his life.
